reuse.why: Instead of extending the shared weekend helper (getDateWithSkippedWeekend) or adding one shared rule, it hand-codes the daily-skip test and weekend filter separately in getNextDate and getUpcomingDates, and leaves budget/schedule-template.ts calling the old move rule.

duplication.why: The 'daily and skipWeekend' predicate plus over-fetch-and-filter-weekends logic is written twice (shared/schedules.ts and server/schedules/app.ts) with different spellings of the frequency check.

placement.why: The getNextDate change sits in shared/schedules.ts where the weekend rule lives, but the parallel copy in the server schedules app is logic that belongs in the shared module.

scope.why: Only the weekend handling and its tests are touched.

maintainability.why: The rule is now split across call sites with inline special-case branches and magic over-fetch counts (7, count*2), and the budget template still applies the old move rule, so the next change must find three places.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and shared/schedules.ts getNextDate each special-case daily schedules around getDateWithSkippedWeekend rather than putting the rule in it; server/budget/schedule-template.ts still calls getDateWithSkippedWeekend directly for daily schedules.

disguised_duplication.where: The daily-weekend-skip predicate and filter appear in getNextDate (frequency?.toLowerCase() === 'daily', take 7, filter/slice 1) and getUpcomingDates (frequency === 'daily', take count*2, filter/slice count): same logic reshaped.

one_place.where: Rule is implemented separately in shared/schedules.ts getNextDate and server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates; server/budget/schedule-template.ts still moves daily weekend occurrences via getDateWithSkippedWeekend.
